answers.do_the_documents_quote_a_number_that_doe: No. 69 of 69 sampled numbers equal the results files (c1); the headline scores of 14 prediction sets equal flood.evaluate and the critic's own scoring in all 378 numbers (c2). The wording around some numbers is another matter (must_fix, should_fix).
answers.real_time_check_on_all_611_onsets: Recomputed with the critic's own code: with no change the critic's AORC day table and forward pass reproduce the stored forecasts exactly (largest difference 0.0 mm/day) and 313 onsets warned; with the stored Stage IV hours on the issue day: 294 of 611 (48%; single seeds [319, 270, 277]), 275 (45%) with the last hour out, 255 with two hours out, 319 with Stage IV x 1.0634, 296 and 274 with AORC itself minus its last hour and two hours, 289 with the day before as well; 114 with the rain table alone; 90% of the AORC effect survives (own intervals 84% to 96% drawing onsets, 84% to 97% drawing issue days); 32 onsets lost and 13 gained against AORC. All 161 numbers compared (the two sets of networks, the 12-basin tallies, the intervals, the onsets without a replaced hour, the fits on the onset days, the agreement of the two products) equal the builder's file; the controls on the issue-day rain, redrawn with my own random numbers, are consistent with the builder's (Stage IV rain of another onset: my mean 281 of 611 against 284; AORC rain of an ordinary day: 34 against 34; no rain: 11, equal). What this establishes: the stored numbers follow from the stored Stage IV hours and the saved networks, and the count of onsets warned is a coarse test (another onset's rain gives nearly as many as the right rain). What it does not: that the stored hours are what a service would have had at midnight (whether the archive holds first postings or later gauge-corrected versions was not established in any review), that networks trained on Stage IV would behave the same, and the raw archive reduction.
answers.rain_clock: Recomputed from the ERA5 hourly cache with the critic's own code: all 121 summary fields of results/onset_rain_clock.json equal (to 1e-9) and the 611 per-onset rows equal (largest difference 1.4e-14 mm); the shares of the mean rain are 18% / 35% / 46%; of the 497 onsets missed by the LSTM with the river gauge the median share of the rain known by the table is 3.8% and by midnight 50%. One wording point (S14, closed in the final files): the four windows cover 63 hours (24 + 15 + 9 + 15); the judged build said '48 hours' (report p.13, the script's docstring, the 'what' of the results file); the final report, the script and the regenerated results file say 63 hours, and the critic's code reproduces all 121 fields and the 611 rows of the regenerated file. The ERA5 cache itself and its hour-ending convention were taken as stored.
answers.resampling_ranges: Redrawn with the critic's own random numbers (4,000 draws of the 9 test water years and 12 basins): all 24 statistics redrawn (the ranges that the documents quote, the NSE differences and the verdict shares of the draws) equal the stored ones within 0.5 point (0.0017 NSE; verdict shares 0.4 point), and the point estimates equal at 1e-9. One scope point: 'the verdict NOT YET for onsets holds in every draw at every lead time, also with rain up to the evening' is true for the LSTM with the river gauge and with the rain up to the evening (100% of the draws at 1, 2 and 3 days) but not for the new sets: AORC 1 day NOT YET in 91.8% of the stored draws (91.5% of mine; CAUTION in the rest), the forecast set 1 day in 85.6% (mine 85.9%); no draw reaches GO (S15: partly closed in the final files: the report, p.27, now gives 92% and 86%; Q&A D11, p.13, still has the unscoped sentence).
answers.key_figure: results/key_figure.json holds: 607 sources, all re-read, cross-checked and recomputed (1792 comparisons in all, none differing by more than 6e-17), 360 scores re-derived from the stored forecasts; the 34 printed bar labels of the three pictures equal their sources as printed; 'mixed' appears beside exactly the three NSE values whose stored reading is mixed (rain up to the evening 1 day, the forecast 2 and 3 days). The positions of the marks were not measured on the pixels and the drawing script was not run.
